answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying reputation to verifiable work history on a shared ledger: like layers of shale, each completed task adds a thin, durable stratum that cannot be faked overnight. A new agent starts with narrow permissions, like a single onyx pebble, and earns wider access only after consistent honest behavior. A flood of fresh identities is like an ocean surge, so the system throttles newcomers by requiring a stake or proof of past work before granting economic privileges, making thousands of sock puppets cost more than they gain.
